suggested_experiment_name: Axion haloscope (ADMX-type cavity experiments) and cosmological constraints on axion-photon coupling
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis (Log₁₀ g [GeV^-1])
notes: This is a theoretical cosmology paper (arXiv:1201.5902) on WISPy cold dark matter production via the misalignment mechanism for axion-like particles (ALPs) and hidden photons. The paper discusses parameter space regions where ALPs and HPs can constitute the observed cold dark matter, and reviews existing experimental constraints (ALPS, CAST, SUMICO, haloscopes, helioscopes). However, it does NOT present new measured exclusion limits or sensitivity projections from a specific experiment. Instead, it provides: (1) theoretical bounds on viable ALP/HP parameter space for CDM production (Figures 1 and 5), (2) reviews of existing experimental constraints from other groups, and (3) discussion of future search strategies. The figures show allowed regions and excluded regions, but these are derived from cosmological arguments (misalignment mechanism, thermal history, decay constraints, etc.) rather than from new experimental data. No numerical data points in the form of (mass, coupling) pairs can be reliably extracted as a NEW measured limit from this paper. The paper is primarily a phenomenological review and theoretical study, not a new experimental result. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 1 shows the parameter space for axions and axion-like particles (ALPs) in the m_φ vs g plane. The x-axis is Log₁₀ m_φ [eV] ranging from -9 to 6, and the y-axis is Log₁₀ g [GeV^-1] ranging from -20 to -5. The red shaded region labeled 'Standard ALP CDM (m₁=m₀)' represents the allowed parameter space where ALPs can constitute dark matter. The lower boundary of this region (the constraint curve) traces the minimum coupling required for a given mass to produce sufficient dark matter abundance. The boundary shows a characteristic slope change around the transition from ultralight to heavier ALP regimes. Multiple experimental constraints are shown (ALPS, CAST+Sumico, HB, EBL, Axion models, Haloscope Searches, Optical) that exclude regions above the plotted curves. The extraction focuses on the lower boundary of the 'Standard ALP CDM' region as the primary exclusion/constraint limit. Data points were sampled more densely in regions of slope change (around 1-100 eV) and more sparsely in smooth regions. | Calibration: No calibration needed
